observations: The top console has a two-tier design, characteristic of the PS4 Slim.
The bottom console has a three-tier design, characteristic of the PS4 Pro.
The brand 'SONY' and model 'PS4' are visible on both units in photo 0.
Two black DualShock 4 controllers are resting on the top console.
Watermarks 'BUCHI_TECH' and 'POSTED ON JIJI' are present on the image.
The consoles show some surface dust and minor wear.

claims.evidence: Requires a photo of the System Information screen showing a jailbreakable firmware version (e.g., 9.00 or 11.00) or a homebrew menu.

claims.claim: ps4 pro with downloaded games inside
claims.evidence: Requires a photo of the console dashboard showing the library of installed games.

risks.risk: Consoles may not power on or have faulty video output.
risks.proof: A video showing both consoles booting to the home screen.

risks.risk: Optical disc drives may be defective.
risks.proof: A video of a game disc being inserted and loaded on both consoles.

risks.risk: The 'hacked' status may be incorrect or the firmware updated.
risks.proof: A photo of the 'System Information' screen for both consoles.

risks.risk: Controllers may have stick drift or button failure.
risks.proof: A video demonstrating the controllers working in the system menu.

proof_requests: Video of both consoles powering on and reaching the home screen.
Photos of the 'System Information' screen for both consoles to verify firmware.
Photo of the home screen showing the installed games.
Video showing a disc being read by both consoles.
response.reason: The items are identifiable as a PS4 Slim and a PS4 Pro from their physical design and visible branding. They will be priced at the worst case (non-functional and unhacked) until proof of operation and firmware version is provided.
